newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: BOLSWESSANEN SEES HIGHER PROFITS IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: BOLSWESSANEN SEES HIGHER PROFITS IN 1997.

text.p: Dutch food and drinks group Koninklijke BolsWessanen NV said on Thursday it expected 1997 operating profits to be higher than in 1996.
"For all four products groups the 1997 operating result is expected to be higher than in 1996," the company said in a statement.
"The executive board expects that, in the absence of unforeseen circumstances, net income per share from ordinary activities in 1997 will increase," it added.

BolsWessanen said it expects its associates' income to grow slightly in the current year but the tax burden is expected to increase and interest charges will also rise as a result of takeovers and joint ventures which were sealed in 1996.

Investments in fixed assets will total 120 million guilders in 1997, slightly down from last year's 122.9 million. The investments will be financed from the company's existing funds, BolsWessanen said.
Earlier, the company posted a 1996 net from ordinary operations of 184.2 million guilders, down 9.2 percent from 1995's 202.9 million.
After a 19.9 million guilder extraordinary charge, the 1996 total net profit was 164.3 million. In 1995, a 2.9 million guilder one-off gain raised the total net to 205.8 million.
Chairman Mac Zondervan told a news conference that restructurings in the company's four divisions would contribute at least five million guilders to 1997 net profits.
BolsWessanen had already announced further restructurings when it published its half-year results last year.
"The costs involved have been charged as extraordinary expenses to the (1996) profit and loss account," it said.
